_comment: Page scaffold created by init. Each page gets its H1, a purpose line and the outline headings. Order = nav order. Sections follow Diátaxis: explanation (getting-started, architecture, modules, workflows, integrations, data, shared, operations, security), reference (generated) and appendices.

pages.title: {{product}} documentation
pages.purpose: What {{product}} is, who uses it, the main journeys, and how to read these docs.

pages.title: Getting started
pages.purpose: Entry point for anyone new to {{product}}.

pages.title: About this documentation
pages.purpose: Scope, sources, conventions, how to search and navigate.

pages.title: Product overview
pages.purpose: The product in business terms: capabilities, objects, lifecycle.

pages.title: Users and roles
pages.purpose: Who uses the system and what each role can do.

pages.title: Navigating the application
pages.purpose: Menus, screens and how users move through the product.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.purpose: Overview of the technical architecture (C4: context, containers, components).

pages.title: System context
pages.purpose: C4 level 1: users and external systems around {{product}}.

pages.title: Solution structure
pages.purpose: C4 level 2: deployable units, projects, folders and their purpose.

pages.title: Application architecture
pages.purpose: C4 level 3: layers, components and conventions inside the main application.

pages.title: Request lifecycle
pages.purpose: What happens from start-up to a rendered response.

pages.title: Data access
pages.purpose: How the code reads and writes data.

pages.title: Front end
pages.purpose: UI technology, scripts, bundling, client-side behaviour.

pages.title: Configuration & environments
pages.purpose: Where configuration lives (key names only, never values) and how environments differ.

pages.title: Scheduled & background jobs
pages.purpose: Everything that runs without a user: schedulers, queues, long-running jobs.

pages.title: Business modules
pages.purpose: One page per functional module, in business language with links into the code.

pages.purpose: End-to-end journeys across modules and systems.

pages.title: End-to-end journey
pages.purpose: The main business journey from request to completion.

pages.title: State machines

pages.title: Integrations
pages.purpose: Every external system, inbound API and machine endpoint.

pages.title: Inbound API
pages.purpose: Every endpoint other systems call: contract, rules, authentication.

pages.title: Machine endpoints & scheduled jobs
pages.purpose: Endpoints called by schedulers and every action that runs without login.

pages.title: Data
pages.purpose: Data stores, model, codes and the database object map.

pages.title: Data model
pages.purpose: Core entities, relationships and patterns.

pages.title: Databases
pages.purpose: Each data store, cross-database links, triggers, deployment.

pages.title: Codes & statuses
pages.purpose: Every code list and status set, checked against enums and seed data.

pages.title: Shared libraries
pages.purpose: Cross-cutting code reused by every module.

pages.title: Base classes & helpers
pages.purpose: Base classes and helper utilities.

pages.title: Services map
pages.purpose: Every service class and its business page.

pages.title: Operations & quality
pages.purpose: Build, environments, deployment, monitoring and constraints.

pages.title: Testing
pages.purpose: Test projects, coverage and gaps.

pages.title: Runbook
pages.purpose: How to set up, run, build, test, deploy and troubleshoot {{product}}, step by step, from the build files (reference: Build and run) and the error catalogue. Key names only, never values.

pages.title: Security
pages.purpose: Security model at a glance.

pages.title: Authentication
pages.purpose: How users and systems sign in.

pages.title: Authorisation
pages.purpose: How permissions are decided.

pages.title: Security findings
pages.purpose: Risk register (SEC-nn): severity, where, impact, recommendation. No secret values.

pages.title: Appendices
pages.purpose: Glossary, defects, coverage and document control.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.purpose: Business and technical terms. Unknown expansions are marked as such.

pages.purpose: Functional defects (DEF-nn) and debt (TD-nn), each verified in code.

pages.title: Document control
pages.purpose: Scope, method, regeneration, conventions, agent access, out of scope.
